demos.name: Barbell Back Squat
cues: Set the bar across your upper back, hands just outside your shoulders, and unrack it with feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your trunk, then sit down and back, keeping your knees tracking over your toes.
Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, then drive through the whole foot to stand.
Keep your chest up throughout; the bar should travel in a straight vertical line.

demos.name: Barbell Bench Press
cues: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar, feet planted, shoulder blades pulled together.
Grip just wider than shoulder-width, unrack, and lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up and slightly back toward the rack, keeping your wrists straight and elbows tucked at about 45 degrees.

demos.name: Barbell Row
cues: Hinge to about 45 degrees with a flat back, holding the bar at arm's length.
Pull the bar to your lower ribs, driving your elbows back.
Lower under control without letting your torso rise.

demos.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Rest the top of your rear foot on a bench behind you, holding dumbbells.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is parallel.
Drive up through the front foot. Complete all reps on one leg before switching.

variants.name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
variants.note: A barbell on your upper back instead of dumbbells.

demos.name: Cable Fly
cues: Set both pulleys at chest height and stand a step forward with a handle in each hand.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in an arc.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.

demos.name: Conventional Deadlift
cues: Stand with the bar over mid-foot, feet hip-width. Hinge down and grip just outside your legs.
Flatten your back, pull the slack out of the bar, and push the floor away.
Keep the bar against your legs the whole way; stand tall without leaning back.
Lower by pushing your hips back first, then bending the knees once the bar passes them.

demos.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
cues: Lie back with a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, palms forward.
Press both dumbbells up and slightly together over your chest.
Lower until your elbows are just below the bench, then press again.

demos.name: Dumbbell Curl
cues: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward.
Curl both dumbbells to your shoulders, elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower slowly. Alternate arms if you prefer.

variants.name: EZ-Bar Curl
variants.note: An EZ bar in both hands.

demos.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
cues: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise both arms out to the side until they are level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly. Lead with the elbows, not the hands.

variants.name: Band Lateral Raise
variants.note: A band under your feet instead of dumbbells.

demos.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
cues: Place one hand and knee on a bench, the other foot on the floor, back flat.
Row the dumbbell to your hip, keeping your elbow close to your body.
Lower to a full stretch. Finish all reps before switching sides.

demos.name: Goblet Squat
cues: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands cupping the top end.
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Sit down between your knees, elbows tracking inside them.
Pause at the bottom, then push the floor away to stand tall.

variants.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
variants.note: Hold the kettlebell by the horns.

demos.name: Hammer Curl
cues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Curl up keeping the palms facing in the whole way.
Lower under control.

demos.name: Hanging Leg Raise
cues: Hang from the bar with straight arms.
Raise your straight legs until they are at least parallel to the floor, curling your pelvis up.
Lower slowly without swinging.

variants.name: Hanging Knee Raise
variants.note: Bend your knees as they come up: easier.

demos.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
cues: Sit with your upper back against a bench and a padded bar across your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso and thighs are level.
Squeeze hard at the top with a neutral chin, then lower under control.

demos.name: Lat Pulldown
cues: Sit with your thighs under the pad and grip the bar just wider than shoulders.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, leaning back only slightly.
Return slowly until your arms are straight and your lats stretch.

demos.name: Leg Extension
cues: Sit with the pad on your shins and your knees in line with the machine pivot.
Extend your legs until straight, pausing at the top.
Lower slowly. Use a smaller range if your knees complain.

demos.name: Leg Press
cues: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad, feet hip-width on the platform.
Release the safeties and lower the platform until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Press back up without locking the knees out hard, and keep your lower back on the pad.

demos.name: Barbell Overhead Press
cues: Hold the bar at your collarbones, grip just outside shoulder-width, elbows slightly in front.
Brace your glutes and trunk, then press the bar straight up, moving your head back out of the way.
Finish with the bar over the middle of your foot and your head through. Lower to the start.

demos.name: Overhead Dumbbell Triceps Extension
cues: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands cupping the top end.
Lower it behind your head by bending only the elbows.
Press back to straight arms; keep your elbows pointing forward.

demos.name: Plank
cues: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, body in a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abs so your hips neither sag nor pike.
Hold for time; stop when your form breaks.

demos.name: Pull-Up
cues: Hang from the bar with palms facing away, hands just wider than shoulders.
Pull your chest toward the bar, driving your elbows down and back.
Lower until your arms are fully straight. Add weight or reps to progress.

variants.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
variants.note: A band under your knees takes some of your weight.

demos.name: Push-Up
cues: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees.
Press back up without letting your hips sag or pike. Elevate your hands to make it easier.

demos.name: Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, dumbbells hanging below your chest.
Raise both arms out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control.

demos.name: Romanian Deadlift
cues: Start standing with the bar at your hips, knees slightly bent.
Push your hips back and slide the bar down your thighs, keeping your back flat.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch (usually just below the knee), then drive your hips forward to stand.

demos.name: Seated Cable Row
cues: Sit tall with feet braced and a slight bend in the knees.
Pull the handle to your stomach, driving your elbows back and chest up.
Let your arms straighten fully without rounding your back.

demos.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
cues: Sit upright with a dumbbell at each shoulder, palms forward.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower until the dumbbells are level with your ears, then repeat.

demos.name: Seated Leg Curl
cues: Sit with the pad above your heels and the thigh pad locked down.
Curl your heels under the seat as far as possible.
Return slowly to straight legs.

demos.name: Standing Calf Raise
cues: Stand with the balls of your feet on the platform and shoulders under the pads.
Rise as high as possible onto your toes.
Lower until your heels drop below the platform for a full stretch.

variants.name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
variants.note: Dumbbells at your sides instead of the machine.

demos.name: Cable Triceps Pushdown
cues: Grip a straight bar on a high pulley, elbows pinned to your sides.
Push the bar down until your arms are straight.
Return until your forearms pass parallel; keep your elbows still.

variants.name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
variants.note: A rope: spread its ends at the bottom.

demos.name: Walking Lunge
cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step forward into a lunge.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, front shin vertical.
Push through the front foot and step straight into the next lunge with the other leg, alternating as you walk.
